output.brief:
The complaints most likely come from contaminated brake fluid, not driver technique, the new pads or the hills. Northfield Motor Services changed fluid on 13 Eastgate vans during the bay closure. Eleven of them used a bulk drum that had taken on water, and those 11 vans are exactly the 11 vans with complaints. Two of them, retested on 24 Sep, had fluid boiling at about 150°C against 255°C for sealed stock. Wet fluid can vaporise on long descents and make the pedal go soft. The same drivers ran Upper Wend in other vans, 141 days, with no brake reports. Tessaro pads were also fitted at Calder Road and in-house, with no complaints from those vans. Northfield warned Larkspur on 25 Sep, and nobody replied.

Do this week: pull the Northfield-serviced vans from service, test and renew their fluid from sealed stock, then return them. LK-214 and LK-227 used a newer drum, so test them first. Drop the plan to discipline drivers, because it would suppress safety reports. Also tell the drivers who reported that they will not be disciplined. Hold off on changing pad supplier. Confidence is high. The main gaps are that I haven't seen Calder's fluid records and haven't tested fluid in the remaining Northfield vans.
